label: yes
controls_available: HAUL is a fixed simplified-mode button that sets the persistent winch state to engaged=true; while active, each 50 ms tick applies +5 upward acceleration followed by 95/100 drag.
COAST is a fixed simplified-mode button that sets engaged=false; while active, each 50 ms tick applies -4 acceleration followed by 95/100 drag, so the cage continues with retained momentum.
The HAUL and COAST buttons remain available while the run is active and are disabled only at terminal/submission. NEW SHAFT and RETRY are administrative controls, not outcome-affecting actions in D.
autonomous_processes: After render, requestAnimationFrame repeatedly catches up the simulation from elapsed task time; each 50 ms physics tick advances without a new agent action.

The cage position and velocity change every tick under the persistent HAUL/COAST setting, drag, gravity, and boundary restitution, so its momentum and relative position continue changing between clicks.
The specimen advances every tick under the generated steady_sinker, darter, floater, or oscillator law, with generated speed, direction, acceleration, and boundary behavior.
The crate becomes spawned at its generated late tick and remains at its generated position; cage/specimen/crate overlap flags and the capture and crate meters update on every tick.

The capture meter drains while the specimen is outside and fills while it is inside; the crate meter fills while the spawned crate is inside. These transitions can end the run in escaped, specimen_only, secured, or timeout status.

grouped_control_modes.name: D_simplified_persistent_winch
grouped_control_modes.scope: All active simplified-mode winch-setting transitions across seeds and task times; this is the single outcome-affecting grouped mode used for the witness.

clause_i.reason: An observation-free q sees only prior button choices and task times. The generator selects different hidden drift laws, initial positions/velocities, and crate spawn positions/times across seeds, so the same I_t can occur when the delayed best setting is HAUL for one visible world and COAST for another. A q cannot distinguish those worlds or choose the required delayed action for every history in C_Delta(D).

clause_ii.reason: Use the configured bounded window W_t^600: six chronological frames over 600 ms. The visible shaft supplies the cage and specimen positions, their displacement/wake trajectory, the active overlap appearance, and the crate's spawn/location. That recent motion is sufficient to estimate target direction and cage momentum and choose the delayed binary command. The source feedback rule itself uses predicted target position/velocity and cage velocity; a screenshot-only policy obtains those quantities from the recent visible trajectory rather than private state.

clause_iii.reason: For a history with the specimen near the active capture band and the cage moving away under the current setting, choose a=HAUL (or the symmetric COAST case while the cage is moving upward). If no new action is supplied for tau=300 ms, six autonomous ticks move both the inertial cage and the drifting specimen; the relative gap can leave the overlap band while success remains possible because the capture reserve is nonzero. HAUL delivered at t+tau then has lower value, or a smaller advantage over no-op, because it must recover the larger gap and momentum after losing capture ticks. The loss is caused by visible shaft-state evolution, not merely by a later deadline.

common_visible_process: The common witness is the changing vertical alignment of the visible drifting specimen and the visible momentum-bearing cage. The specimen's wake and successive positions reveal its motion, while the cage's successive positions reveal retained velocity. During the same process, a timely HAUL/COAST choice preserves overlap and a delayed choice arrives after the target/cage relationship and capture reserve have degraded.

pre_run.reason: There is no separate start gate: render initializes the winch in COAST and immediately schedules the autonomous simulation loop. If preparation is allowed before the first autonomous tick, the only outcome-affecting preparation choice is one persistent binary setting, HAUL or COAST; no later changes are allowed by the pre-run definition. A reproducible probe of 512 generated difficulty-4 simplified instances found zero secured runs with constant COAST and zero with constant HAUL (COAST: 409 escaped, 101 timeout, 2 specimen_only; HAUL: 384 escaped, 126 timeout, 2 specimen_only). Thus the threshold is not met; the probe rate is not generalized to a population percentage.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 4 activates the narrow 800-unit cage, all four drift laws, 50 ms ticks, 1,000 maximum ticks, 3-sample wake, late crate, and capture/crate meter rates; simplified mode is fixed HAUL/COAST buttons; observation is 600 ms with 6 frames and a 90-second play allowance.
Each generated instance chooses a law, speed, initial position and direction, and darter schedule from the active difficulty pool.
Every tick advances the specimen and inertial cage, spawns the crate at its generated tick, tests overlap, updates both meters, and can change terminal status.
The binary control incorporates cage retained velocity and a six-tick target lead, showing why the next setting depends on current target/cage motion.
The certified reference controller changes the winch no more than once per 600 ms observation window and alternates specimen and crate allocation based on the capture reserve.
The browser replay uses the same specimen/cage physics, and a simplified click records a persistent HAUL/COAST transition after catching up elapsed ticks.
The visible implementation renders the moving cage, specimen, crate, wake positions, crate spawn state, and overlap state on each tick.

Difficulty 4 with simplified interaction creates fixed HAUL and COAST buttons, initializes COAST, and starts the requestAnimationFrame tick loop immediately; full keyboard controls are a separate branch.
The shaft visibly moves the cage and specimen, displays the specimen wake dots, reveals the crate on spawn, and marks active overlap states.
The console exposes the two mutually exclusive simplified button states and visualizes the engaged/coast setting.
The authoritative replay advances the same physics per tick and grades overlap-driven meter evolution and terminal status.
The grader requires the exact simplified interaction source/phase transcript and exact terminal replay, so HAUL/COAST transitions are outcome-affecting and not presentation-only.
The task verifier loads the exported result and invokes the independent Ballast Lantern grader.

The implementation solver makes the same target-lead feedback decision at the configured 600 ms cadence; its private-state access is used only as implementation evidence, not as screenshot information.

uncertainties: The complete generated motion law and future darter schedule are private; the bounded-window claim uses only the currently visible trajectory and averages over future hidden variation as required by the definition.

The browser does not render numeric meter readouts, so a normal screenshot-only policy infers reserve from visible overlap and elapsed task behavior; the real-time witness does not depend on reading a private meter value.
